item.title: France: crowds fill Marseille's Old Port in anti-racism protest
item.description: Hundreds of people gathered at Marseille's Vieux-Port on Monday evening to protest against racism following a deadly shooting near Paris. Police estimated the crowd at 800, while organisers put attendance at more than 1,000.

item.title: Turkey-Libya maritime boundaries deal 'remains null and void,' Greek foreign minister says
item.description: The joint statement responded to the recent decision by Libya's House of Representatives to ratify the 2019 memorandum.

item.title: Trump says Brazil election looked 'rigged' without giving evidence
item.description: The Trump administration has hailed a recent wave of right-wing election victories across South America.

item.title: Microsoft offers around 60,000 employees voluntary buyouts
item.description: The offer will be made available to employees on select teams across the US, Canada, India and the United Kingdom "at level 70 and below," meaning some senior staff could be included. Around 60,000 employees are reported to be eligible.

item.title: Anthropic's IPO filing shows off soaring revenues as the company warns of AI's 'risks to humanity'
item.description: Anthropic warned AI could bring "catastrophic or existential risks to humanity" if it is not "developed, deployed, and operated with appropriate safeguards, oversight, and security measures."

item.title: María Corina Machado seeks talks with Delcy Rodríguez after return from exile
item.description: After a year in exile, Venezuela's opposition leader returns, ready to negotiate with the government. The EU welcomes her and calls for free and fair elections.

item.title: Pope Leo XIV confirms Latin America trip after recovering from surgery
item.description: The Vatican says the Pope is recovering well and will be able to visit Uruguay, Argentina and Peru from 6 to 17 November, with doctors ruling out any complications that could derail the trip.

item.title: Russia: flames engulf buildings after Ukrainian drone attack in Voronezh region
item.description: At least two people were killed and 17 injured in a Ukrainian drone attack on Russia's Voronezh region. Flames engulfed buildings, while falling debris struck a commuter train.

item.title: Zelenskyy calls out monthlong wait for Hegseth to sign off on Patriot missiles
item.description: Kyiv has repeatedly pressed the need for more interceptors to be delivered to its forces as Ukraine continues to defend against deadly Russian missile attacks and jet-powered drone strikes.

item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this October 26th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: UK: Oxford Street pedestrianisation begins in central London
item.description: Pedestrians have taken over part of London's Oxford Street as a new traffic ban comes into force.

item.title: Exclusive: EU to give Frontex new powers to deport migrants from outside Europe
item.description: Under new rules, the EU border agency will be allowed to transfer migrants between third countries, expanding its operations beyond Europe and facilitating deportations from return hubs.

item.title: EU set to miss 2030 marine protection targets, auditors warn
item.description: Despite designating 14% of its waters as protected areas, the EU has placed less than 1% under strict protection, leaving marine ecosystems vulnerable to damaging fishing practices and putting its 2030 biodiversity targets at risk.

item.title: Dictionary.com reveals 2026 Word of the Year - and it's a depressing one
item.description: The internet slang term / suffix "Maxxing" has officially been selected by Dictionary.com as its 2026 Word of the Year.

item.title: Swedish government blocks ChatGPT and Claude. Here’s why
item.description: The ban on employees using browser-based versions of ChatGPT and Claude took effect on Monday 26 October amid security concerns over data processing.

item.title: Cyprus signs $1.8bn deal to develop first gas field, with exports to Europe via Egypt
item.description: The deal is a key step towards harnessing Cyprus' natural gas reserves and bolstering energy cooperation in the Eastern Mediterranean, with exports to Europe via Egypt and production due to start in 2028.

item.title: From the Mecca defence pact to Tehran talks: Is the Middle East’s security landscape shifting?
item.description: Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey are pursuing talks with Tehran while strengthening their military readiness under the terms of the Mecca Defence Alliance.

item.title: ‘Hybrid weapon of war’: Why climate disinformation could be a growing public health threat
item.description: “Climate disinformation is not only a problem of false rumours and mistruths; it is also a problem of power, incentives and accountability.”

item.title: 'Pure garbage': Elon Musk’s AI-generated 'The Odyssey' clip ridiculed online
item.description: The AI slop clip has been blasted online, with many calling it out as "garbage" and an "utter waste of time and money like most of Musk Inc."

item.title: Serbia’s student victory raises hopes of an EU reset
item.description: The Student List’s election win ends Vučić’s 14-year rule and raises hopes of an EU reset, but its stance on Russia sanctions and Kosovo leaves Brussels cautious.

item.title: First international flight arrives at the new Western Sydney airport
item.description: Sydney’s new 24-hour airport has welcomed its first international passengers with the opening described as a ‘milestone that has been decades in the making’.

item.title: 'Yes Bibi or No Bibi': Netanyahu's political future overshadows Israel's election
item.description: Israel's upcoming legislative election could reshape the country's political future amid deep divisions over Benjamin Netanyahu's leadership. Former government spokesperson Eylon Levy tells Euronews what is at stake and why another war with Iran may be imminent.

item.title: Lula’s comeback puts brakes on Latin America’s rightward surge
item.description: Brazil’s re-elected leader now faces a hostile Congress at home and a Trump administration that had bet heavily on his rival.

item.title: Temu falls into line as EU backs its action plan after €200m fine
item.description: The Chinese-owned online retailer has promised stronger action to address several violations of the EU’s Digital Services Act, the European Commission said on Monday, following a €200 million fine in May.

item.title: The architectural heritage of Greece's Kea island: Vibrant colours, stone houses and watermills
item.description: Kea has around 2,500 permanent residents, and despite the growth of tourism, the island has managed to retain its traditional character.

item.title: Olive trees irrigated with treated wastewater, a pilot project to combat drought
item.description: Olive trees irrigated with treated wastewater: in Puglia, southern Italy, a pilot project thus combats drought and emerging pollutants. The molecule is generated by combining hydrogen peroxide and ultraviolet rays. The results of this experience will be known in two years.

item.title: How a Belgian founder built a tech company and a waffle brand in Macao
item.description: Belgian entrepreneur Jérémy Artan de Saint Martin builds a tech firm and waffle brand in Macao, calling the city a land of endless possibilities.

item.title: Ukraine: Russian strikes hit Odesa and Zaporizhzhia, injuring four
item.description: Russian overnight strikes injured four people in Zaporizhzhia and sparked fires in the Odesa region on Monday. Ukrainian emergency services said an industrial site was hit twice more as firefighters battled the flames.

item.title: German business confidence rises in October despite global economic risks
item.description: Germany's ifo Business Climate Index rose in October, driven by stronger manufacturing confidence, although higher energy prices and interest rates continue to pose risks to the economic recovery.

item.title: Ebola: Uganda restricts travel as Nigerian case evacuated to Europe
item.description: The Ebola outbreak that began in the Democratic Republic of Congo in May, now the fastest-growing and most widespread on record, has caused nearly 10,000 confirmed cases across Africa.

item.title: Claude bypassed paywall to access US election data without being asked, days before midterms
item.description: The incident is the latest in a string this year that has raised concerns over Big Tech’s ability to maintain control of its increasingly autonomous AI models and curb their rogue behaviour.

item.title: New business projects decline despite rising foreign investment, UN says at World Investment Forum in Doha
item.description: Foreign investment is rising, but fewer new projects are being announced and funding remains concentrated in a few economies. At the World Investment Forum in Doha, officials and investors are discussing how more countries can benefit and create jobs.

item.title: Algeria approves troop deployment to Niger: what is their mission?
item.description: This rare move comes amid strengthened security ties between Algeria and Niamey following the thwarting of an attempted coup in Niger in August.

item.title: Airbnb changed its check-out chore rules – and hosts are fuming about it
item.description: Some are calling for a boycott of the short-term rental platform after hosts were banned from asking guests to strip bed linens or do the washing up.

item.title: Yeast or famine: Australian convicted murderer loses bid to eat Vegemite in prison
item.description: A convicted murderer has lost a legal bid to overturn a ban on Vegemite in Victoria's prisons, despite his claims that the ban was unlawful because it denied him his human right to enjoy Australian culture.

item.title: Japanese company to compensate users hit by cyberattack
item.description: GMO Internet, a Japanese internet infrastructure company, will compensate customers for losses from unauthorised trading linked to a cyberattack on its cloud service, and will make a ¥5,000 (€28) goodwill payment to every customer currently using the affected service.

item.title: Zelenskyy's planned Brussels visit for peace talks cancelled
item.description: Zelenskyy said the planned visit would gather Ukraine, the US, EU and NATO in high-level talks on security guarantees and diplomatic efforts to end Russia's war against Ukraine.

item.title: Galp and Moeve fail to agree merger of refining and distribution operations
item.description: Portuguese multinational energy corporation Galp confirmed that talks with shareholders of major Spanish energy firm Moeve, to merge downstream operations, have collapsed, and says the result will not affect its operations.

item.title: Trump officials back Orbán bid for UN secretary-general, WSJ reports
item.description: Trump administration officials are reportedly floating former Hungarian prime minister Viktor Orbán for UN secretary-general, potentially backed by the US, Russia and China, though nothing is confirmed and his selection remains uncertain.

item.title: Why Israel’s wartime election isn’t just about the battle with Iran and Hamas
item.description: From army exemptions for the ultra-Orthodox to a stalled 7 October inquiry, the issues splitting voters have little to do with Gaza, Lebanon or Iran.

item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this October 26th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Be nice, not nasty: Nobel laureate Geoffrey Hinton on why AI needs humans at its heart
item.description: Nobel Physics prize winner Geoffrey Hinton is widely regarded as one of the godfathers of artificial intelligence, but he's spent much of the last few years warning against its potential dangers. He discussed those ideas at Starmus and also revealed why 'The Terminator' is his favourite film.

item.title: November 2026 travel guide: Where to go, what to see and the new hotels to book in Europe
item.description: From early Christmas markets in Vienna to late-autumn sunshine in the Canary Islands, November offers plenty of reasons to plan a European escape before the festive rush.

item.title: Revolut to launch platform for investing in private tech companies
item.description: Revolut announced on Monday the launch of Revolut Ventures, a new platform developed with Carne Group to give eligible investors access to private technology companies, an investment market traditionally reserved for wealthy individuals and large institutions.

item.title: One in three young adults use AI chatbots for drug and alcohol information, study finds
item.description: Researchers warn that chatbots could spread misinformation about substance use, as a survey finds that one in three young adults in the United States are turning to AI for drug-related information.

item.title: Oil plunges more than 6% from near wartime highs as diplomacy over Iran seemingly gathers pace
item.description: Brent crude fell more than 6% on Monday morning, retreating from its highest close since March, as regional mediators headed to Tehran and US President Donald Trump weighed a deal with Iran, while investors braced for a week packed with central bank decisions and earnings reports.

item.title: 2.92-metre monster fish: German angler lands giant catfish from Polish reservoir
item.description: Oliver Schäfer from the Eifel and his fishing partner landed a 2.92-metre catfish at a tournament in Poland. The fish is already well known among anglers.

item.title: Mexico: spectacular Catrina parade brings the dead to life
item.description: Skeleton faces, extravagant headdresses and dazzling costumes transformed Mexico City's streets into a colourful spectacle. The annual Catrinas Parade celebrates the country's Day of the Dead traditions.

item.title: Why are Elvis Presley rightsholders suing AI company Anthropic?
item.description: Anthropic could face more than $40million in damages over the alleged unauthorised use of Elvis' music catalogue.

item.title: 'Democracy has won': Europe celebrates Lula's surprise victory in Brazil
item.description: European leaders have greeted Lula's re-election in Brazil. "Democracy and multilateralism have won in Brazil," Ursula von der Leyen said.
